Olivia (CSM): Quick sync — PhoenixHealth QBR next Tue 11am PT. Need a one-page account health, onboarding friction points, token econ snapshot, and a short cost-action slide. Who picks up cost + forecast?

Ethan (FinOps): I'll own cost. Plan to pull 90d baseline, highlight 30d spike days, and produce a 10-week conservative forecast. Any single jobs driving the spike?

Sasha (SE): Yes  nightly ETL run that vectorizes ~2M docs at 02:00 UTC. It caused two quota overages last month. I have the manifest and a proposed stagger/cache fix.

Noah (Sales): Renewal talk in 3 weeks. CFO explicitly asked for a mitigation plan and an example reserved capacity quote. They'll want to see immediate wins pre-renewal.

Olivia (CSM): Ok owners: Ethan = cost + forecast; Sasha = tech root cause + demo; Noah = renewal asks. I'll capture onboarding feedback and propose a "starter kit".

metrics-bot: export: phoenixhealth_tokens_3189999999.csv uploaded to s3://exports/phoenix/3189999999.csv

Ethan (FinOps): Uploaded chart summary: https://files.redwood/phoenix/3189999999/90d_trend.png. Key note: two overnight runs (dates attached) account for ~38% of peak-week tokens. Recommend: 1) embed TTL=7d caching 2) int8 quantization for batch model 3) 80% daily alert + auto-throttle.

Sasha (SE): Demo plan: reproduce nightly job in staging and show before/after with caching + shard staggering. I'll run staged commands and post perf numbers. Snippet I'll show in deck:

```
# run 4 shards staggered
for s in 0 1 2 3; do
  sleep $((s * 20))
  ./vectorize --shard=$s --batch-size=128 &
done
```

Noah (Sales): CFO asked: can we provide p99 latency for Hosted vs Dedicated and a rough reserved quote table (3 commit levels)? I'll draft slide.

Ethan (FinOps): I'll add a Hosted vs Dedicated cost delta table and an estimate for savings at each commit. Also will include a suggested short-term credit bridge if they move to Dedicated.

Olivia (CSM): Onboarding feedback: tickets show two recurring themes: "no starter configs" and "unclear default quotas." I'll propose a Starter Kit with recommended batching defaults, cache rules, and quota guardrails.

metrics-bot: alert: created rule phoenix-daily-cap-80pct (id: ar-3189999999)

Sasha (SE): Quick caching middleware example to include in the starter kit:

```
# simplified cache (node)
if (req.type === 'embed') {
  const key = sha256(JSON.stringify(req.input))
  const cached = await cache.get(key)
  if (cached) return cached
  const out = await callEmbed(req)
  await cache.set(key, out, { ttl: 7 * 24 * 3600 })
  return out
}
```

Ethan (FinOps): Preliminary numbers from the sim: caching + quantization reduces peak token usage ~42% and estimated monthly spend drop ~28% in conservative scenario. I'll attach the CSV.

Noah (Sales): Adding asks list: 1) temporary daily cap + 80% alert 2) reserved capacity quote (3 levels) 3) 30-day optimization SLA (we implement quick wins). Will draft bullets by Mon EOD.

Olivia (CSM): Deadlines: Ethan cost deck + CSV by Mon 2pm; Sasha demo perf + screenshots by Tue 8:30am; Noah draft exec asks by Mon EOD. Dry run Tue 10:15. Any blockers?

Sasha (SE): One tradeoff to call out: if they go Private/VPC some managed cache layers may require extra setup. I'll add a one-paragraph mitigation and an action item to scope local Redis connector.

Ethan (FinOps): Confirming console can surface per-route and per-key cost breakdown; I'll grab a blurred screenshot for the deck.

Olivia (CSM): Perfect  I'll compile onboarding ticket snippets to include verbatim feedback and the Starter Kit checklist. Ping me when assets are uploaded. :sparkles:
